wu: Pet Charades: Students take turns acting out pet actions (e.g., barking like a dog, meowing like a cat) while others guess. Teacher asks 'What pet is it?' and students respond 'It's a dog/cat/bird/fish.'
wuAlt: Pet Flashcard Race: Two teams race to match pet flashcards to their names on the board.
Pet Sound Bingo: Teacher calls out pet names, students cover the matching animal picture on their bingo sheet.
pres: Teacher shows a stuffed dog and says 'I have got a dog.' Then asks a student 'And you?' to elicit 'I have got a...' Teacher uses flashcards to model 'I have got a cat/dog/bird/fish.' To check understanding, teacher holds up a fish and asks 'Have you got a fish?' Students respond 'Yes, I have' or 'No, I haven't.'
presAlt: Pet Family Photo: Teacher brings in a family photo with pets and says 'I have got a dog and a cat.' Students point and repeat.
Pet Survey Demo: Teacher surveys 3 students with 'Have you got a pet?' and writes answers on the board.
prac: Find Your Pet Partner: Each student gets a pet flashcard. They walk around asking 'Have you got a...?' When they find a match (e.g., two dogs), they high-five and sit down. Teacher monitors and corrects pronunciation of 'got' and question intonation.
pracAlt: Pet Memory Game: Students match pet flashcards to 'I have got a...' sentence cards in pairs.
Pet Circle Drill: Students stand in a circle, pass a pet toy, and say 'I have got a...' then pass to the next student who adds a new pet.
ls: Teacher reads a short story about a boy who has a fish. Students listen and raise their hand when they hear the word 'fish.' After, students draw the fish in their notebook to show comprehension.
re: Pet Freeze Dance: Teacher plays music, students dance. When music stops, teacher calls out a pet (e.g., 'bird!'), students freeze and flap their wings like a bird. Last student to freeze is out.
prod: Pet Care Card Project: In groups, students create a care card for a pet (dog, cat, bird, or fish). They write 2-3 imperatives like 'Feed it twice a day' and 'Don't give it chocolate.' Groups present their cards to the class.
rw: Reading and Writing: Students read a short paragraph about 'My Cat' and circle all the imperatives (e.g., 'Brush it', 'Play with it'). Then, they write 2 sentences about how to care for their own pet using 'Feed' or 'Don't feed.'
st: Teacher reads the story 'The Lost Parrot' about a boy looking for his pet bird. After, students sing the goodbye song 'If You're Happy and You Know It' with actions like 'clap your hands' and 'stomp your feet.'
g: Students mark off pets on their bingo sheet as the teacher calls them out.
Teacher says 'Simon says feed the dog' and students pretend to feed a toy dog.
Students act out pet actions for others to guess.
Students ask 'Have you got a...?' to find a matching pet partner.
Students match care instruction cards to the correct pet picture.
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write a 4-sentence paragraph about their dream pet.
Support / weaker learners: Trace over pre-written imperatives like 'Feed the dog' and draw a picture.
hw: Interview a family member: 'Have you got a pet?' and write down 2 answers.
Draw a picture of your family's pet and write 1 care instruction.
Make a pet care card for a friend's pet with 2 rules.
tip: Use the Green March (Moroccan holiday) to connect by discussing pets in families—many Moroccan families have cats or birds, making the theme relatable and culturally relevant.
